findings.source: HoneyFactory.sol:345-350 for (uint256 i = 0; i < registeredAssets.length; i++) { amount = refAmount * weights[i] / 1e18; amount = vaults[registeredAssets[i]].convertToAssets(amount); honeyToMint += _mint(registeredAssets[i], amount, receiver, true); }
findings.issue: The basket loop is split into an outer 'while True' and an inner loop whose header is the overflow test of 'honeyToMint += ...' (e <= c + e), whose exit only reaches the Panic(17) revert; the real bound i < registeredAssets.length is tested inside as 'if d + 1 >= registeredAssets.length: return'. The first iteration's prefix is printed before the loops.
findings.rule: As for c00557's claimComp: never use as a while condition a test whose exit edge reaches only a revert; print it as a require in the body and use the remaining exit test (d + 1 < registeredAssets.length) as the loop condition.

findings.decompiled: mem[96] = _1061 / mem[64] = this.address / mem[44] = caller << 96 / mem[12] = 0x23b872dd... / call registeredAssets[d + 1].transferFrom(address sender, address recipient, uint256 amount) with: args Bytes(12, 0), caller << 96, Bytes(20, this.address), _1061 ... _969 = uint96(mem[84 len 12]) / mem[uint96(mem[84 len 12])] = 0x6e553f65...
findings.source: SafeTransferLib.safeTransferFrom(asset, msg.sender, address(this), amount) and safeApprove (scratch-space encoding, then 'mstore(0x34, 0)' / 'mstore(0x60, 0)' restores)
findings.issue: The name of transferFrom is found but its arguments print as a byte concatenation that crosses word boundaries instead of (caller, this.address, _1061); after safeApprove restores the high bytes of the free-memory pointer with mem[52] = 0, the pointer prints as uint96(mem[84 len 12]) and the deposit call that follows falls back to raw memory.
findings.rule: Before printing call arguments of a known signature, regroup the argument bytes into 32-byte words: Bytes(12, 0) ++ first 20 bytes of (x << 96) is address(x), and the 12 zero low bytes of x << 96 ++ Bytes(20, y) is address(y). After 'mem[52 len 32] = 0', mem[64] == uint96(mem[84 len 12]) when bytes 64..84 are known zero; keep the name mem[64] (or its last value).

findings.issue: A read of the whole slot 1 whose every use is address(_3) is printed as stor[1] although def storage names slot 1 feeReceiver and the write two lines below uses the name.
findings.rule: When every use of a full-slot read is masked to a named field's bits, print the field name (_3 = feeReceiver).
